sections.subheading: Why one LED per well solves the uniformity problem
body: WPI is built around a problem every high-throughput photochemistry screen runs into: getting the same light to land on well 1 and well 24 equally. A single light source spread across a plate almost never manages it. Twenty-four individual LEDs, one per well, each with its own optical guide and lens, does.

Illumination comes from below rather than above, running straight through a transparent plate or vial bottom. That same bottom-up design lets 4 mL auto-sampler vials drop directly into the plate format when the workflow calls for it, without switching to a different instrument.

Heat management runs on two fronts at once: the anodized aluminum body dissipates heat passively, and an integrated cooling fan keeps operating temperature stable through longer experiments, important with 24 LEDs running simultaneously rather than one.

sections.title: One LED Per Well: Uniform Illumination Design
sections.description: Uniform illumination across 24 wells is harder than it sounds, and it comes down to a design choice most instruments don't make: giving every well its own dedicated light source instead of sharing one across the whole plate. Each LED pairs with a custom optical guide and lens that aims it directly into its corresponding well, keeping neighboring samples from picking up stray light meant for the well next door. Illuminating from below lets that light pass efficiently through a transparent plate or vial bottom, and because the design already works with standard plate geometry, dropping 4 mL auto-sampler vials into the same format extends that same precision to a different sample workflow entirely.

sections.title: Wavelength Selection and PWM Intensity Control
sections.description: Getting the right wavelength is only half the job in a screening experiment. The other half is controlling intensity without accidentally changing the wavelength that was just selected.
body: Nine wavelength options cover near UV through far red, plus lime and cool white as broad-spectrum choices, all fully characterized so exactly what's being delivered is never a guess. The optional PWM dimmer module solves the intensity problem specifically: instead of reducing current to dim the LED, which can shift its emission wavelength, PWM adjusts the duty cycle, how long the LED stays on during each rapid switching cycle, so spectral output stays exactly where it started even as irradiance changes.
